result.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, stable termination, and dead-end/frontier facts across the closed FCSTM. The dominant behavior-consequence findings are: (1) the CollisionAvoidance composite and its two substates are unreachable from root in the closed model despite being semantically required operating behavior, which also makes the collision_avoidance_deactive->collision_avoidance_active and collision_avoidance_active->collision_avoidance_deactive event consumers unreachable (declared but not reachable), violating NL12-INITENTRY-1, NL12-ENDPOINT-1/GUARD-1, NL13-ENDPOINT-1/GUARD-1 at the coverage/reachability layer even though the local transitions exist; (2) HighwayMode and UrbanMode both retain exact outgoing self-loop/cross-mode transitions after reaching FinishState-adjacent states, and the FinishState endpoint itself has an outgoing '/enter_' self-loop back into [*] re-entry semantics and cross-mode continuation via HighwayMode<->UrbanMode wrapper-level R45RouteToken transitions, raising a stable-termination concern for NL6-TERMINATION-1 and NL10-TERMINATION-1 since the composite HighwayMode/UrbanMode can still route back into active operation (R45RouteToken==23/24/26/27 branches) after 'ending'; (3) the enter_hwy/lane_change guard_disjointness issue (NL3-DISJOINT-1) is confirmed: both cruise and lane_change alternatives from enter_hwy carry the identical guard 'dist_to_front_25_extra_lane_true' with no distinguishing condition, which is an operational indistinguishability defect independent of endpoint existence.

issues.strongest_rebuttal: These wrapper-level transitions are compiler-synthesized route-token machinery for representing composite-to-composite mode switches (HighwayMode<->UrbanMode) rather than authored continuations after termination; if compiler-owned route bookkeeping is excluded per working_contract attribution policy, the underlying author-level termination intent might still hold. This is preserved as a candidate because the exact closed-model transitions remain reachable regardless of their generation origin.

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, stable termination, and dead-end/frontier facts across the closed FCSTM. The dominant behavior-consequence findings are: (1) the CollisionAvoidance composite and its two substates are unreachable from root in the closed model despite being semantically required operating behavior, which also makes the collision_avoidance_deactive->collision_avoidance_active and collision_avoidance_active->collision_avoidance_deactive event consumers unreachable (declared but not reachable), violating NL12-INITENTRY-1, NL12-ENDPOINT-1/GUARD-1, NL13-ENDPOINT-1/GUARD-1 at the coverage/reachability layer even though the local transitions exist; (2) HighwayMode and UrbanMode both retain exact outgoing self-loop/cross-mode transitions after reaching FinishState-adjacent states, and the FinishState endpoint itself has an outgoing '/enter_' self-loop back into [*] re-entry semantics and cross-mode continuation via HighwayMode<->UrbanMode wrapper-level R45RouteToken transitions, raising a stable-termination concern for NL6-TERMINATION-1 and NL10-TERMINATION-1 since the composite HighwayMode/UrbanMode can still route back into active operation (R45RouteToken==23/24/26/27 branches) after 'ending'; (3) the enter_hwy/lane_change guard_disjointness issue (NL3-DISJOINT-1) is confirmed: both cruise and lane_change alternatives from enter_hwy carry the identical guard 'dist_to_front_25_extra_lane_true' with no distinguishing condition, which is an operational indistinguishability defect independent of endpoint existence.
